title: Contain kernel-assignment oscillations under mixed-quant bursts and add safety layers
creator: Aisha Patel
description: After the scheduler autotuning change (optimize-probe-window), we observed sustained kernel assignment oscillations during mixed-quant traffic bursts. Oscillation caused repeated kernel switches, KV-cache thrashing, and p95/p99 latency spikes for several mid-sized customer workloads. This ticket contains containment steps, short-term mitigations, and long-term action items to prevent recurrence.
incident_summary: On 2026-02-28 a scheduler heuristic intended to improve cold-start latency (speculative probe window widening) began amplifying kernel probing under mixed-quant workloads. Combined with a recent attention autotile patch that reduced per-worker headroom, workers entered a cycle of kernel recompile/eviction -> KV cache miss -> backpressure -> scheduler probing. Observable impact: p95 latency increased 1.8x for multi-tenant hosts and several Dedicated customers experienced transient request throttles.

impact: Intermittent but high-severity latency regressions affecting multi-tenant hosts and Dedicated customers. Several production jobs experienced timeouts; one enterprise customer reported degraded UX. No data loss or correctness regressions observed.
root_cause: Two changes interacted: (1) scheduler speculative probing widened its probe window and did not account for mixed-quant kernel affinity, leading to concurrent kernel probing on hot workers; (2) an attention autotile memory optimization reduced worker headroom enough that kernel swaps triggered recompiles/evictions rather than warm transitions. The combined effect amplified KV cache misses and forced repeated kernel selection churn.
mitigations_applied: Disabled 'optimize-probe-window' feature flag cluster-wide for affected regions
Introduced a temporary knob to prefer 'stable' kernel variants for pinned customer models
Rate-limited speculative probe concurrency to 1 probe per worker per 30s
Ramped Dedicated pool capacity and increased autoscale headroom for impacted teams
Backported scheduler patch to honor kernel-quant-affinity metadata and avoid probing incompatible kernels
followup_action_items: Telemetry: add per-worker kernel-transition histogram and kv-cache-hit-rate per kernel variant (owner: Marcelo, est: 3)
E2E tests: add mixed-quant burst scenario to CI harness to catch regression windows (owner: Priya, est: 5)
Scheduler: implement 'probe budget' with adaptive backoff and per-model affinity constraints (owner: Kofi, est: 8)
Runtime: add preflight kernel compatibility check to avoid heavy recompiles under low-headroom (owner: Linh, est: 5)
Console: dashboard tile and alerts for kernel-churn-rate > threshold (owner: Sara, est: 2)
Create canary policy: run new scheduler heuristics only on fenced canary hosts with synthetic mixed-quant load (owner: Infra Eng, est: 3)
Post-deploy checklist: include KV-cache warmup verification and headroom check before enabling autotile optimizations (owner: Runtime Eng, est: 2)
Run capacity fencing experiment for Dedicated customers to ensure isolation from noisy multi-tenant probing (owner: Capacity Team, est: 5)
Documentation: update deployment playbook and runbook for kernel-flapping incidents (owner: Docs, est: 2)
Retrospective: schedule blameless postmortem review with affected customers and CS (owner: Aisha, est: 1)
acceptance_criteria: Kernel-churn-rate for production hosts remains below 0.5 transitions/minute under synthetic mixed-quant bursts
p95 latency for affected models returns to baseline within 15% across canary and prod regions
CI mixed-quant scenario fails if scheduler introduces more than X probes per worker in 60s
Canary policy prevents rollout to >5% of capacity until telemetry shows stability for 72 hours
notes: This incident highlights the common failure mode when two orthogonal optimizations reduce safety margins independently. Future autotuners must be evaluated with synthetic adversarial traffic patterns. We should consider a staging environment that simulates mixed-quant production ratios for all runtime changes.
